strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Loop
strategies.desc: Directly follows the reference pattern with 8 sequential all-reduce dispatches, each preceded by local bidiagonal coupling and followed by uncoupling. Total 8 all-reduce dispatches with full W*S payload each. Represents the naive approach with maximum dispatch count but simplest logic.

strategies.name: Fused Bidirectional Coupling Kernel
strategies.desc: Combines the forward coupling and backward uncoupling operations into single local compute kernels between all-reduces, reducing memory traffic by eliminating intermediate buffer writes. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but with fused local ops that may enable better compiler optimization and reduced device-host synchronization points.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Replace each full all-reduce with reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing each rank to compute only its shard's coupling dependencies during the scatter phase. Requires 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but each operates on smaller payloads (W*S/W for RS, scaling up for AG), potentially better network utilization at scale.

strategies.name: Pipelined All-Reduce with Async
strategies.desc: Issue multiple all-reduce operations asynchronously where dependencies allow, overlapping communication of stage i+1 with local computation (uncoupling/coupling) of stage i. Uses async dispatch primitives (xm marks) to hide latency, keeping 8 all-reduce calls but with potential wall-time reduction through comm-compute overlap.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc:
Exploit potential multi-node structure (num_nodes parameter) by first performing intra-node reductions on smaller groups, applying coupling transformations on intermediate results, then inter-node reductions. Requires careful data layout but can reduce cross-node traffic by factor related to nodes, trading more dispatches (16-24) for smaller cross-node payloads.
